meta.title: FA - the COSMOS file-access service, and the QFORM encoding its bodies use
meta.purpose: The protocol behind tasks 38, 23 and 33 - pull, create and the sync daemon. All three are proved against a real machine, so most of this is MEASURED; it is written down so the next change is made against a statement rather than a re-reading of the captures.
meta.authority: This file and the C# must agree - the conformance tests assert the parts a machine can check.
meta.layering: An FA message is the BODY of a SINTRAN datagram (see sintran-wire.json). Its first eight bytes are a fixed prefix; everything after is QFORM, EXCEPT a data message, which is raw content to the end.
meta.one_line: remote files - open, read, write, create, list - and the QFORM encoding its bodies use

status_values.MEASURED: Observed on the wire, with the capture or live run named.
status_values.INFERRED: Follows from something measured, not itself observed.
status_values.UNKNOWN: Copied or mirrored. Never computed or varied.
status_values.SUPERSEDED: Believed once, disproved. Kept so it is not re-derived.

qform.summary: How FA writes its fields down. Each item is a tag byte saying what KIND of thing follows and how long it is, then the thing itself. A body reads as a list of pairs - a selector naming a field, then that field value - and a selector of 0x00FF marks the end.

traps.name: a flat walk descends into constructed values
traps.detail: Reading a body as a flat run of tag/value pairs walks INTO a class-0 payload and reads its bytes as top-level tags.
traps.evidence: measured against captures; QformReader recurses instead

traps.name: SINTRAN pads a body to an even length
traps.detail: The pad byte can look like the start of a field. On 2026-08-06 it was read as an escaped length, ran off the end and threw, and every listing request was refused until it was found.
traps.evidence: DOC/captures; the fix is the single-trailing-byte guard in QformReader

message_prefix.summary: The eight bytes before the QFORM, present on every FA message.
message_prefix.qform_starts_note: Not a field - the offset where the tagged data begins. It was listed as a field with a width of nothing, which a generator would have emitted as an empty member.

data_transfer.note: A data message is the eight-byte prefix then RAW content to the end - it carries no QFORM. It is recognised by its LENGTH and by a transfer being in progress, never by parsing it: walking it as tagged fields decodes file text as tags.

rules.name: bodies must be WORD-ALIGNED
rules.detail: an odd-length body is dropped in silence by the peer
rules.evidence: found the hard way; see the memory of the same name

rules.name: the last message is marked AND counted
rules.detail: the flag is used, but the byte count decides completion - a misread flag would otherwise hang a write forever

open_questions.question: Why does a LIST-FILES against our FA server put D100 into a reconnect loop?
open_questions.observed: D100 opened six conversations in thirty seconds. We issued a NEW connection number on each confirm - 0x0042 through 0x0047 - while every 'I am finished' from D100 named 0x0042.
open_questions.candidate: the client may keep its OWN conversation number rather than adopting the one we hand out, in which case issuing a fresh one per connect is our error. NOT diagnosed - the numbers are what was observed, the reading of them is not established.
open_questions.would_settle_it: a capture where a real client reconnects to a real server - every archived FA capture holds a single session
open_questions.progress_2026_08_17: The two-number scheme is now MEASURED - see conversation_numbers. What is still unknown is narrower: on a RECONNECT, does the server issue a new number or reuse the old one? Our pool hands out a fresh one each time (0x0042..0x0047 in thirty seconds) while D100 kept naming 0x0042.

pull_a_file.title: Reading a file off a remote machine
pull_a_file.summary: The ladder task 38 drove against D100. Every step was answered by the real machine.
pull_a_file.proved: task 38 - 20400 bytes pulled off D100, SHA256 identical to the original

steps.note: we know the service by NAME, not address
forwarding SPENDS one of the server's free slots
from here we have its address and XROUT is out of the way

steps.loop: until the whole file has arrived

steps.note: raw content, 1024 bytes a block - NO tagged fields

gotchas.name: A repeat is not a new event.
gotchas.detail: A retransmitted confirm must not rewind the session - treating one as a fresh step restarts the transfer.

gotchas.name: Filter by session port.
gotchas.detail: Another conversation on the same node will otherwise be read as part of this one.

create_and_push_a_file.title: Creating a file on a remote machine and writing to it
create_and_push_a_file.summary: The ladder task 23 drove. The name is QUOTED, which is what makes it a create rather than an open of something existing.
create_and_push_a_file.proved: task 23 - 20400 bytes written to D100 under a quoted new name, the size confirmed by D100's own file server

steps.note: name in quotes, plus how many pages
now open the file we just made
the raw block; the LAST one is marked AND counted

gotchas.name: Bodies must be WORD-ALIGNED.
gotchas.detail: An odd-length body is dropped in silence by the peer - no error comes back, the transfer simply stops.

gotchas.name: Quotes are what create.
gotchas.detail: The quoting is kept on the wire; an unquoted name asks to open something that already exists.

conversation_numbers.summary: There are TWO, one per direction, used like port numbers: each side addresses the other by the OTHER side's number.
conversation_numbers.evidence: claude-delete-file-102-to-100-2026-07-29.pcapng, a real ND deleting a file on another real ND

observed.confirm: 07d2 0002 0048 - the server issues 0048 and echoes the client's 0002
observed.client_to_server: 07f0 0048 ... - the client addresses the server by the SERVER's number
observed.server_to_client: 07f0 0002 ... - and the server answers using the CLIENT's

conversation_numbers.does_not_settle: F3. That capture holds ONE session, so it cannot show whether a RECONNECT should be given a fresh number or keep the old one - which is exactly what our reconnect loop turns on.

byte_string_form.rule: COMPACT while the field is 15 bytes or fewer - the length rides in the tag's low nibble - and ESCAPED from 16, where it needs a following byte.
byte_string_form.evidence: a real client's OpenFile carries BF with fifteen characters and switches to B0 10 at sixteen; every captured delete is compact (BB, BD, BF)
byte_string_form.why_it_matters: emitting the compact tag for a longer field is not a size error, it is a DIFFERENT ENCODING - the peer then reads the wrong number of bytes

file_name_field.rule: the name, the SINTRAN terminator 0x27, then ONE more byte - so the field is the name length plus two
file_name_field.evidence: four samples across two capture sets
file_name_field.the_extra_byte: UNKNOWN and it VARIES - T, W, F, R across the four. Not constant, not padding (odd-length three times), not derivable from the name. We write a space and stop at the terminator when reading, which is what a real server must also do or it could not accept four different values.
